scope.excluded_work: all catalog problems and research tracks other than #021/B7, #022/B2, and #023

question: Can a graph-equivalent correction-bit fault-vector encoding turn PyMatching's supported public decode interface into a lower-tail single-stream decoder without changing a correction?

known_before_preregistration.disclosure: the deterministic graph scan proved graph signature equality and correction-vector geometry using all-zero inputs only; no nonzero frozen-corpus candidate prediction, timing vector, speedup, tail verdict, or classification has been observed

candidate_contract.baseline: the frozen sparse private C++ decode_to_edges_array path plus complete edge-to-component preindex
candidate_contract.candidate: a graph-equivalent matching object whose fault IDs encode detector and observable correction bits, decoded through public Matching.decode and applied with vectorized XOR
candidate_contract.graph_equivalence: for every window, normalized edge endpoints, weights, and error probabilities must exactly match the baseline graph; only fault-ID payloads may differ
candidate_contract.fault_vector_encoding: contiguous detector-output IDs followed by observable-output IDs over the parity union of every committed component's correction support
unchanged: distance-6 circuits, noise, 1,000-round horizon, and frozen X/Z corpora
two-pass correlated matching topology, weights, probabilities, and correlation groups
arrival order, correction propagation semantics, logical frame, and residual checks
single-stream execution with no shot batching
one-microsecond p99 and one-percent miss thresholds

corpus_contract.timed_order: sparse baseline then public candidate on even shots and public candidate then sparse baseline on odd shots

timing_contract.raw_vectors: sparse baseline total plus public fault-vector candidate total and all six candidate phases as base64 little-endian uint64 nanoseconds
timing_contract.relative_score: sparse-baseline p99 divided by public-candidate p99 for X and Z, aggregated by geometric mean only after the semantic veto

classification_rule.rule: after the semantic veto, select the first candidate stage failing p99 <=1 microsecond per committed layer and miss fraction <=1 percent in either basis: public decode, vectorized correction apply, commit residual check, then candidate end-to-end
classification_rule.interpretation: a supported public API removes the private-interface boundary but remains a same-host diagnostic and cannot by itself prove a hardware deadline

kaggle_inspired_evaluation.verification_veto: candidate predictions, residuals, corpus hashes, graph equivalence, and output maps must pass before a speedup is credited
kaggle_inspired_evaluation.reference_relative_cost: sparse-baseline direct p99 divided by public-candidate direct p99 per basis
kaggle_inspired_evaluation.aggregate: geometric mean across X and Z
kaggle_inspired_evaluation.absolute_guardrail: a relative improvement cannot waive the absolute tail and miss limits

hard_boundaries.reason: the candidate uses a supported API but remains same-host Python software, not a QPU, controller, asynchronous device link, or hardware feedback path

execution_guard.preflight_before_publication: real graph reconstruction, exact graph-signature equality, complete output-map verification, and all-zero syndrome only; zero nonzero frozen-corpus candidate predictions and zero candidate timing observations
